_comment: Emulator configuration for A-G0 and C-G0. Parameter names are those of pulser.noise_model.NoiseModel in pulser 1.9.1. Units follow Pulser: rates in 1/us, temperature and trap_depth in uK, waists in um, detuning_sigma in rad/us.

ideal.backend: certisample.rydberg.Subspace (see g0_spec v3), validated against pulser_simulation.QutipEmulator
ideal.device_reason: AnalogDevice has no DMM in pulser 1.9.1; MWIS weights require local detuning
ideal.hamiltonian_convention: H = sum_i Omega(t)/2 X_i - sum_i (Delta(t) + eps_i Delta_dmm(t)) n_i + sum_{i<j} C6 / r_ij^6 n_i n_j
ideal.dmm_weights: eps_i = 1 - w_i (DMM subtracts detuning; heavier vertices receive less penalty)

noisy.status: deferred: exact noisy emulation is infeasible at 20 atoms; the noisy backend is specified in a later version before any noisy data. Noise values below are retained as the intended model.
noisy.run_design: runs = 20 with samples_per_run = 1 gives every one of the K = 20 proposals its own noise realization

value_mapping.dephasing_rate: 1 / T2, T2 = 20 us (conventional reading; verify against Pulser's dephasing_rate definition before freezing)
value_mapping.temperature_trap_depth_trap_waist: T = 20 uK, U_trap = 150 uK, w_trap = 1 um; together they set atom-position noise

omitted.dmm_sigma: set to 0: no published DMM noise value exists in the source (its benchmark used no local addressing). This is a known limitation for the MWIS arm, whose weights are encoded through the DMM.
omitted.detuning_hf_psd: omitted: the source states the high-frequency detuning power spectral density values are confidential
omitted.leakage: omitted, as in the source, where it is expected to be subleading
omitted.amplitude_and_detuning_offsets: omitted, as in the source's complete noise model

noisy.source_of_values: H. Erbin, P.-L. Burdeau, C. Bertrand, T. Ayral, G. Misguich, 'Many-body Quantum Score: a scalable benchmark for digital and analog quantum processors and first test on a commercial neutral atom device', arXiv:2601.03461 (2026), Appendix B.1. The authors state the parameters were provided by Pasqal and characterized in different experiments, lie in the ranges describing neutral-atom QPUs, may vary in time and between machines, and were not characterized on the Ruby machine directly. These are therefore representative neutral-atom values, not device-specific Fresnel specifications; device-specific values require Pasqal Cloud access.
